An Instagram professional account on its own, without a Facebook page.

## Connect accounts

Each person connects their own Instagram account in the Gateway, once, and every app that asks uses it. Apps never see the tokens. [How connecting works](/docs/connect-oauth)

The redirect URI to register, with your Gateway's address (like `apps.example.com`):

```text
https://<your gateway>/connect/instagram/callback
```

The Instagram API with Instagram Login, on a Meta app. The token lasts an hour; the long-lived exchange isn't done by the Gateway. Not yet tried against a live connect.

1. Open [developers.facebook.com](https://developers.facebook.com/apps) and create an OAuth app (also called a client or an integration).
2. Add the redirect URI above.
3. Copy the client ID and client secret. The secret is often shown only once.

Add it to your Gateway. It asks for the client ID and secret:

```bash
everyapp provider add instagram
```

Or add it in **Manage workspace → Providers**.

### Use it in an app

```ts
capabilities: {
  instagram: { access: "read", scopes: ["insights.read"], why: "What the app does with it." },
},
```

Apps ask for these scope sets:

| Set | Allows | Provider scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | Instagram account (who you are) | `instagram_business_basic` |
| `insights.read` | Insights (read) | `instagram_business_basic`, `instagram_business_manage_insights` |
| `posts.write` | Posts and comments | `instagram_business_basic`, `instagram_business_content_publish`, `instagram_business_manage_comments` |

**Check it worked:** `everyapp provider show instagram` shows the client as set. Then open the account menu → **Connected accounts** → **Connect Instagram**.

Something wrong or missing? [Open an issue](https://github.com/every-app/every-app/issues/new?template=provider-request.yml&title=Provider%20guide%3A%20Instagram).
